Root cause: in update_fee (app/routers/fees.py), changing amount or product_amount only sets those fields. balance_amount is never recalculated, so an unpaid fee keeps its original total (100 + 25 = 125) instead of the new one.

Proposed fix: capture the old total before applying the updates. If amount or product_amount changed and the fee is not PAID, shift balance_amount by the change in total. Paid fees are left alone, and an explicit balance_amount in the request still takes precedence. This preserves any partial payment already reflected in the balance. The existing status logic runs unchanged afterward.

The regression test now passes, and so does the full tests/ suite.

Root cause: in `update_fee` (app/routers/fees.py), changing `amount` or `product_amount` only set those fields. `balance_amount` was never recalculated, so an unpaid fee kept its original total (100 + 25 = 125) after the amount changed.

Fix: the patch records the old total (`amount + product_amount`) before applying the updates. If `amount` or `product_amount` changed, the request has no explicit `balance_amount`, and the fee is not PAID, it shifts `balance_amount` by the change in total. This keeps any partial payment already reflected in the balance. Paid fees are left at zero. The existing status logic runs unchanged afterward.
